sections.title: Authentication review — function-level flow and remaining risks
sections.html:
Function / boundaryLogic and connection
AuthService.register / auth.registerSchema normalizes inputs; service checks email and hashes password, commits unverified customer; route directly enqueues verification email. Queue failure is swallowed after account commit. User can call resend API, but current frontend has no resend action. This path is not protected by the durable business notification outbox.
verify_emailDecode audience-specific token → undeleted user → reject already verified → update+commit → issue access and create hashed refresh session → second commit → cookie. Failure between commits may leave verified account without returned session; sign-in is recovery. Parallel verification and deletion interactions need native tests.
loginLookup email → dummy hash on missing identity → Argon2 verification → email verification → admin TOTP only if enabled → optional rehash/last-login update → access claims and refresh session → commit. Route's claim all admins require TOTP is broader than implementation. User/session creation locks do not alone prove earlier credential reads remain fresh.
refresh_token / SessionRepositoryHash cookie; identify owner; lock/reload active User; lock/recheck unexpired session; delete old token; create new hash; build current-role/version access; commit. Shared user-before-session order protects deletion/refresh in the inspected two-interleaving test.
logoutDelete refresh row and commit first; then Redis blocklist access JTI; clear cookie only after service success. Redis failure can leave partially completed logout. Frontend refresh-before-logout can then fail on the deleted cookie. Preserve honest reporting while designing a local-clear/recovery path.
forgot_password / reset_passwordGeneric response hides existence in body; eligible user gets signed reset token and best-effort enqueue. Reset consumes Redis NX marker before DB change, then replaces hash, increments version, deletes sessions, commits. DB failure after marker claim consumes the link without completing reset; marker loss/eviction weakens single-use assumptions. Distinct reset tokens and account deletion/password races require native tests.
Two change_password servicesFrontend intends CustomerService via /customers/me/change-password: lock/reload active user, verify current hash, SQL auth_version+1, revoke sessions. Legacy /auth/change-password uses AuthService: nonlocking initial read, Python cached-version increment. Need deterministic concurrent login/reset/change/delete verification; no reproduced race is claimed.
setup_totp / verify_and_enable_totpAdmin role gate; first stores generated secret disabled, next verifies code and stores enabled. No fresh-password challenge, active-user lock or session-version bump in these methods. Secret stored as plain String at application layer. Enrolment/enable races, recovery, replay controls and deployment key/encryption policy remain review candidates, not demonstrated account takeovers.
Google start / finish / wrapperGenerate state/nonce/S256 PKCE, Redis10-minute binding and browser cookie → consume once → exchange code with15s timeout → fetch signing keys → validate identity claims → reject automatic email linking and privileged roles → create hashed refresh → fixed frontend redirect. Failure wrapper rolls back, hides provider details and clears state cookie. UI strips error/query hints and confirms only through session restore.
Security/logging helpersRS JWT purposes/audiences and token-version reload provide independent checks; revocation fails closed. Password Argon2 is synchronous in async service, requiring load measurement before recommending offloading. Log scrub masks email arguments; synthetic control passed. No secrets were read or copied.

Test scope: existing auth/security/native deletion-refresh tests were read, not rerun. Offline audit helper ran synthetic schema/IP/redaction probes only, with settings import explicitly prohibited. It intentionally asserts current defect behavior; it is not the desired application regression suite.

sections.title: Customer/privacy review — invariants and follow-up
sections.html:
AreaReviewed behavior / connections
Profile and addressesCurrent identity scopes operations. Active-user lock serializes profile/create/update/default against deletion; addresses capped10. Clear-default and target updates share transaction. Deleting an address scopes ownership but does not acquire user lock; race outcomes require evaluation, not automatic vulnerability claims. Most optional None values mean no change, not clear. Avatar upload holds user lock during provider operation, with rollback/orphan cleanup pending further review.
ReviewsCreation checks product existence and optional owned order/item; only delivered/completed order gives verified-purchase badge. Unique(user,product) backs one review. Edit returns review to pending; delete queues image cleanup; aggregate recomputation locks Product. Public product route first validates product visibility, but separate /customers/reviews/product route delegates directly to approved-review listing: visibility parity needs explicit policy/test. Votes reject self/nonapproved, unique insert prevents repeats, counters increment atomically; concurrent moderation/vote races pending.
WishlistRedis set,90-day TTL; read filters unpublished/hidden/deleted/inactive-seller products. No actual DB fallback despite comment. Set order is not chronological and added_at is product creation time, not wishlist insertion time. One image query per product and no size limit in reviewed add path: measure/define semantics before repair. Arbitrary cache corruption can raise UUID parsing errors.
PreferencesCustomer legacy field names map explicitly to shared NotificationService preference names. This eliminates a separate source of truth at these callers; the destination service, worker selection and legacy backfill remain pending audit.
DeletionLock/reload customer; verify local password; block active orders, open returns/disputes and pending refunds. Transaction records cleanup manifest and removes permitted profile/notification/review text/images, sessions/addresses while retaining identity key/financial evidence and ratings. Version increment invalidates access. OAuth-only users are told to set password; supported secure setup/recovery journey needs verification. Seller/admin managed offboarding remains deliberately gated.
External cleanupOutbox event retains retryable assets. Worker requires deleted user, clears cache with timeout, validates allowed bucket/exact owner path and generated UUID.webp, checks shared references, deletes only attributed assets. Uncertain ownership enters operator review. Full outbox retries and concurrent new shared references remain unverified; no storage objects were deleted.

Next audit slice: complete frontend API-to-mounted-route comparison, then notification outbox/recovery and customer privacy race tests, followed by order/payment/refund/wallet/stock invariants. The new-chat handoff should prioritize F13 among repairs after review scope is agreed.

sections.title: Architecture and control/data flow
sections.html:
LayerPurpose and connection
React entry and providersmain.tsx → App.tsx. App composes error boundary, authentication, guest access, cart and saved-item providers. Layout hosts customer, seller and admin routes. Individual role screens are UI gates, not server authorization.
Frontend transport/contractsapi/client.ts sends same-origin/proxied API requests with cookies and an in-memory bearer token. Domain helpers validate runtime payloads and exact decimal strings. GET may refresh once; writes are never automatically replayed by transport.
FastAPI outer stackCORS → security headers → request ID → error boundary → request logging → rate limiter → router/dependencies/handler. Error responses use a common envelope. The rate limiter generally sees client IP before route auth supplies identity.
Authentication and ownershipapi/deps.py verifies JWT/revocation, reloads current user role/version/verified state, and resolves active/onboarding sellers. Services and repositories must separately scope resource IDs. Admin ownership bypass is helper-specific, not universal permission.
Services and repositoriesRoutes validate contracts and delegate operations. Services enforce workflow and commit/rollback boundaries. Repositories construct SQL and locks. Models/schema/migrations jointly define constraints; no single layer proves concurrency safety.
Persistence and runtime policyPostgreSQL stores orders, seller orders, payments, wallets, returns/disputes, notification outbox and settings. Runtime policy merges validated SystemSetting overrides with startup defaults. Redis supplies rates, revocation/cache and ARQ queue coordination.
Workers/integrationsARQ registers notification, expiry, settlement and cleanup jobs. Durable DB notification state is dispatched/retried separately from queue execution. PayFast, Google, Supabase and Resend are external trust/availability boundaries; local mocks do not certify them.

Dependency listings below are import/syntactic-call navigation. They are not a resolved runtime call graph; callbacks, DI, dynamic imports and asynchronous jobs require manual tracing.

sections.title: Workflow map and invariants for the next reviewer
sections.html:
Authentication and session lifecycle

AuthProvider restores refresh-cookie state, requests /auth/me, and stores access token only in memory. api/client deduplicates refresh and uses sessionVersion to reject obsolete refresh results. Backend dependencies reject stale role/auth-version/deleted or unverified accounts. Sign-out refreshes then logs out before clearing local identity. Verify invalid-cookie/logout recovery and account-switch races before changing this behavior. Do not copy tokens or real environment values into this report.

Guest/account checkout

UI obtains an authoritative quote, then stores only an owner-scoped UUID recovery capability before submitting a reviewed payload. Unknown outcomes retain the same key/payload; explicit recovery finds the committed order. A recovery404 must not permit a new key while an original request can arrive late. Guest tokens are carried in memory or explicit access controls, not public URLs. Backend quote, reservation, coupon and order locks still need a fresh end-to-end source review.

Payments

PayFast is hosted checkout: server token → explicit browser form → callback → authoritative provider reconciliation. A callback hash alone does not prove paid amount/currency. The reconciler checks basket/transaction identity, amount, currency and state, records evidence, and may correctly leave state unchanged for manual review. Admin reconciliation uses order_id, whereas refund/detail operations commonly use payment_id. COD approval, delivery and cash collection are separate states.

Returns, refunds and seller money

Return approval is not receipt; receipt is not a refund transfer. A pending refund reserves refundable amount; confirmation records externally transferred money and applies the existing accounting/stock reversal rules. Dispute resolution in favor of a customer may approve a return but does not send money. Seller withdrawal request reserves funds; payout approval does not debit again, rejection releases once, and completion records a receipt, not a bank transfer. Historical records, shortfall accounting and mixed-operation races need source/evidence review; never infer settlement correctness merely from a successful HTTP response.

Admin settings

Seven runtime business fields are editable, with validation, changed-fields-only submission and before/after review. New UI sends a full expected snapshot; server serializes even missing-row overrides with a PostgreSQL transaction advisory lock and rejects stale state. Optional snapshot preserves legacy callers. Settings do not include provider keys or enablement. Consumers may use saved snapshots or current policy differently; trace this before changing hold/timeout/commission rules.

Notifications and privacy

DB outbox and worker registry exist; keep_result=0 avoids retaining sensitive original job args in ARQ results. Failed-event operator APIs exist but lack a frontend. Customer deletion is limited cleanup with retained financial/dispute evidence; final retention and seller/admin offboarding must not be invented. Read actual lifecycle/cleanup services and approved privacy policy before changing anything.

sections.title: Candidates requiring investigation — not confirmed bugs
sections.html:
• AuthProvider.signOut refreshes first and only clears after successful logout. Verify the user recovery experience for expired/revoked refresh cookies and offline/server failures; distinguish honest revocation reporting from inability to locally exit an unusable session.
  • config.py startup commission is strictly0<rate<1, while runtime admin schema permits0 and1. Trace zero-net/zero-commission ledger constraints and business policy before judging the discrepancy.
  • PaymentService.reconcile_payfast holds order/payment locks during provider HTTP requests. Measure contention versus expiry/fulfilment and timeout behavior; do not remove locks without preserving state integrity.
  • Caller-supplied request IDs lack an explicit length/format guard in RequestIDMiddleware. Assess log/header limits and whether upstream validation suffices.
  • Normal rate limiting is per client IP and fails open on Redis outage. Confirm acceptable abuse controls and monitoring; do not silently change availability policy.
  • Admin write forms keep uncertainty markers across reloads. They intentionally prevent automatic repetition, but operators need a documented reconciliation/recovery path; do not add a blind reset button.
  • Guest COD validateOrder checks fewer identity fields than PayFast. Trace all display/access callers and malformed-success tests before deciding severity.
